{
  "rules": [
    "If sentiment history shows increasing positive sentiment (e.g., >0.20) over recent days, model should not over-forecast; adjust downward to avoid overshoot.",
    "When true outcome shows strong upward trend (e.g., >+5% from prior day), model often under-estimates the magnitude — increase forecast slope or add early momentum buffer.",
    "If model forecast is flat or slowly rising while true outcome spikes, reduce forecast lag by accelerating early response to recent highs.",
    "After a sharp spike in true outcome, model often over-anticipates — apply a ‘cool-down’ rule: reduce forecast slope by 10–20% for next 3–5 days post-spike.",
    "If sentiment is neutral or negative (0.00–0.10), model should not assume upward bias — forecast should reflect mean reversion or slight downward drift unless strong catalysts exist.",
    "Model tends to overfit recent history when sentiment is low — reduce forecast sensitivity to recent 3–5 day data if sentiment < 0.10.",
    "When true outcome exceeds model forecast by >10% for 2+ consecutive days, apply ‘mean reversion correction’ — reduce forecast by 5–10% for next 3–5 days unless sentiment confirms continuation."
  ]
}
